speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any sputum? If so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: I've been dealing with this cough for over six months, and yes, it produces white phlegm. It seems to get much worse at night and makes it hard for me to keep up with my usual physical activity. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration and the white phlegm suggest a chronic condition; have you noticed any wheezing, chest tightness, or a history of smoking? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to check for structural abnormalities or infiltrates.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of the lungs, flattened diaphragms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray showing hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms is highly suggestive of obstructive lung disease. Have you noticed a history of smoking or exposure to dust and chemicals? Additionally, do you experience symptoms like finger clubbing or cyanosis?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been smoking one pack a day for the past 20 years, and I work as a delivery driver so I'm often around exhaust fumes. I haven't noticed any changes to my fingers or lips, though I do feel quite winded when I try to keep up with my usual pace. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
